question: With no complete round supplied, making one birth at a time under laws that read nothing of a next round, does the ring that returns still return: in every order, or under a priority read from the structure whatever way ties are broken; and does it return more slowly in births as the parts it has given off pile up?
inputs: The registered starts, serial laws, priorities and seeds; the shared definitions; ticket A's engine for the complete rounds.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; any outcome of this study before the freeze; for the engine's author, the pilot's programs.
primary_observable: Whether each run builds the same to depths 1, 2 and 3 as the complete rounds; its returns and the moves between them.
comparators_or_controls: The cohort law; ROUND-FREE's present-state law and its order effect; the complete rounds of ticket A.
resource_budget: The grid of 19,200 runs through the shared runner, at most 16 GB and one row in the long-running index; everything else under ten minutes.
first_executable_signal: Row G of the predictions table.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column.
stop_rule: The study stops when its registered runs are done and each prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of laws changed by hand (assumption A224) and of starts built by hand; every census and sample is finite and proves no all-size statement; no claim about ordinary growth beyond the cited records, and none about time, minds or living things.
